title: During, for, in, over, throughout; by and until
summary: Предлоги времени **for / during / over / throughout / in**, различие **while** и **during**, а также **by** (срок) и **until** (продолжительность до момента).
ru:
## for, during, over, throughout: как долго и когда
Эти предлоги отвечают на разные вопросы, и поэтому они не взаимозаменяемы.
- **for** + отрезок времени отвечает на «как долго?»: *for three weeks*, *for most of the evening*, *for ages*. После for всегда идёт **мера времени**.
- **during** + событие или период отвечает на «когда?»: *during the war*, *during the meeting*, *during my stay*. После during стоит существительное, называющее период или событие, но не количество времени: ~~during three weeks~~ → **for** three weeks.
> I've worked here **for** ten years. — Я работаю здесь десять лет.
> Prices dropped **during** the recession. — Цены упали во время рецессии.
> Someone coughed **during** the speech. — Во время речи кто-то кашлянул.

## over и throughout
**over** + период — «на протяжении, в течение», часто с оттенком изменений и развития: *over the past decade*, *over the summer*, *over the weekend*. **throughout** подчёркивает «от начала до конца, без перерыва» — как во времени, так и в пространстве.
> The company has grown steadily **over** the last five years. — За последние пять лет компания неуклонно росла.
> She sat in silence **throughout** the meeting. — Она молчала всё совещание от начала до конца.
> Tea is grown **throughout** the region. — Чай выращивают по всему региону.

## in, within и «за какое время»
**in** + срок показывает, сколько времени занимает действие (*She wrote the essay in two hours* — за два часа) или через сколько оно произойдёт (*in ten minutes*). Так же **in** используется со словами «последний, первый, лучший» (в значении «за время»): *the best film I've seen in years*, *the coldest winter in a decade*. Для «не позже чем за» подходит **within**: *within a week*.

## while или during
- **while** + подлежащее и сказуемое: *While I was waiting, I read the paper.*
- **during** + существительное: *During the break, I read the paper.*
> ~~During I was abroad, my flat was rented out.~~ → **While** I was abroad, my flat was rented out.
> ~~While the break, I read the paper.~~ → **During** the break, I read the paper.

## by и until: «не позже» и «до тех пор»
Это один из самых частых источников ошибок у русскоязычных, потому что по-русски оба значат «до».
- **by** — срок, к которому действие должно быть **выполнено** (не позже): *Please send it by Friday.* (в пятницу уже должно быть отправлено)
- **until / till** — действие **продолжается** вплоть до момента: *I'll be here until Friday.* (я здесь всю неделю, в пятницу уйду)
- **by the time** + clause — «к тому моменту, как»: *By the time we arrived, the film had started.*
- **not ... until** — «только тогда» (подчёркивает позднее наступление): *It wasn't until 2010 that she moved abroad.*
- **till** — разговорный вариант until; в начале предложения и в формальном стиле обычно until.
> Hand in your essay **by** Monday. — Сдайте эссе не позже понедельника.
> The library is open **until** 9 p.m. — Библиотека открыта до 9 вечера.
> I didn't realise it was a mistake **until** I read it again. — Я понял, что это ошибка, только когда перечитал.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~I've lived here during five years.~~ → I've lived here **for** five years.
- ~~The report must be ready until Friday.~~ → ready **by** Friday.
- ~~I'll wait by 6 o'clock.~~ → I'll wait **until** 6 o'clock.
- ~~The food was awful during all the trip.~~ → **throughout** the trip / **during** the whole trip.
en:
## for, during, over, throughout: how long and when
These prepositions answer different questions, so they are not interchangeable.
- **for** + a length of time answers "how long?": *for three weeks*, *for most of the evening*, *for ages*. After for comes a **measure of time**.
- **during** + an event or period answers "when?": *during the war*, *during the meeting*, *during my stay*. After during we use a noun that names a period or an event, not an amount of time: ~~during three weeks~~ → **for** three weeks.
> I've worked here **for** ten years.
> Prices dropped **during** the recession.
> Someone coughed **during** the speech.

## over and throughout
**over** + a period means "across" or "during", often suggesting change and development: *over the past decade*, *over the summer*, *over the weekend*. **throughout** stresses "from beginning to end, without a break" in both time and space.
> The company has grown steadily **over** the last five years.
> She sat in silence **throughout** the meeting.
> Tea is grown **throughout** the region.

## in, within and "how long it takes"
**in** + a period shows how long an action takes (*She wrote the essay in two hours*) or when it will happen counting from now (*in ten minutes*). We also use **in** after first, last, best and similar words: *the best film I've seen in years*, *the coldest winter in a decade*. **within** means "no later than": *within a week*.

## while or during
- **while** + subject and verb: *While I was waiting, I read the paper.*
- **during** + noun: *During the break, I read the paper.*
> ~~During I was abroad, my flat was rented out.~~ → **While** I was abroad, my flat was rented out.
> ~~While the break, I read the paper.~~ → **During** the break, I read the paper.

## by and until: "no later than" or "up to"
This pair causes trouble for many learners because both can be translated as "до" in Russian.
- **by** gives the deadline by which something must be **done**: *Please send it by Friday.* (it must already be sent on Friday)
- **until / till** shows that something **continues** up to a point: *I'll be here until Friday.* (I stay all week and leave on Friday)
- **by the time** + clause means "at or before that moment": *By the time we arrived, the film had started.*
- **not ... until** stresses that something happened late: *It wasn't until 2010 that she moved abroad.*
- **till** is informal; at the start of a sentence and in formal writing we usually prefer until.
> Hand in your essay **by** Monday.
> The library is open **until** 9 p.m.
> I didn't realise it was a mistake **until** I read it again.

## Common mistakes
- ~~I've lived here during five years.~~ → I've lived here **for** five years.
- ~~The report must be ready until Friday.~~ → ready **by** Friday.
- ~~I'll wait by 6 o'clock.~~ → I'll wait **until** 6 o'clock.
- ~~The food was awful during all the trip.~~ → **throughout** the trip / **during** the whole trip.
structure:
## Сравнительная таблица
| Слово | Что стоит после | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|---|
| for | мера времени | как долго | for two hours · for years |
| during | событие или период (сущ.) | когда, в ходе | during the interview |
| while | подлежащее + глагол | пока, в то время как | while I was driving |
| over | период | на протяжении (с развитием) | over the last decade |
| throughout | период или место | от начала до конца; повсюду | throughout the year · throughout the country |
| in | мера времени | за какое время; через сколько | in an hour · in years |
| within | мера времени | не позже чем | within a week |
| by | момент времени | не позже (срок) | by Friday · by then |
| until / till | момент времени или клауза | вплоть до (продолжается) | until midnight · until I call |

## Формулы
> **for** + 3 hours · **during** + the lecture · **while** + I was working
> finish **by** Friday (срок) · work **until** Friday (до пятницы включительно)
> **by the time** + clause · **not ... until** = только тогда

exercises.title: for, during, throughout, over, by или until?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: She has lived in Osaka {{for}} three years.
The festival is held {{throughout}} the country, from the north to the south.
Prices have risen sharply {{over}} the past five years.
I'm staying with friends {{for}} the next two weeks.
We were not allowed to talk {{during}} the exam.
Please submit the application {{by}} 5 p.m. on Friday.
The shop stays open {{until}} midnight on Fridays.

exercises.title: while, by, until, in
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: {{While}} I was abroad, my flat was rented out.
{{During}} my stay in Lisbon, I visited three museums.
I won't know the results {{until}} next week.
The documents must be signed {{by}} the end of the month.
She finished the whole report {{in}} two hours.
It was the first time {{in}} years that I had felt relaxed.
{{By}} the time we arrived, the show had already started.
It wasn't {{until}} I got home that I realised I had lost my keys.

items.q: I've been learning Spanish ___ six months.
___ she was waiting, she read a magazine.
items.why: После слова стоит клауза (she was waiting) — **While**.

items.q: Can you finish this ___ Thursday? I need it for the meeting on Friday.
We kept in touch ___ the summer by email.
The Wi-Fi was unreliable ___ the conference.
I'll wait here ___ you come back.
items.why: До тех пор, пока не... — **until** + клауза.

options: I worked in a bank during three years.
I worked in a bank for three years.
I worked in a bank while three years.
Don't leave until I come back.
Don't leave by I come back.
Don't leave during I come back.
She was ill while the holidays.
She was ill during the holidays.
She was ill at the holidays.
He has published five books in the last decade.
He has published five books while the last decade.
He has published five books by the last decade ago.
items.why: **in the last decade** с present perfect.

options: The project will be completed until next March.
The project will be completed by next March.
The project will be completed for next March.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение по образцу в задании.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **during**: While the film was on, nobody spoke.
answers: During the film, nobody spoke.
Nobody spoke during the film.
During the film nobody spoke.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **while**: She called me during the time I was cooking dinner.
answers: She called me while I was cooking dinner.
While I was cooking dinner, she called me.
While I was cooking dinner she called me.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **by**: Hand in the essay no later than Friday.
answers: Hand in the essay by Friday.
Hand the essay in by Friday.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **until**: I'll stay at the office and leave at 8 p.m.
answers: I'll stay at the office until 8 p.m.
I will stay at the office until 8 p.m.
I'll stay at the office until 8 pm.
I will stay at the office until 8 pm.
I'll stay at the office until 8.
I will stay at the office until 8.
I'll stay at the office till 8 p.m.
I will stay at the office till 8 p.m.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **throughout**: The noise continued from the beginning to the end of the film.
answers: The noise continued throughout the film.
The noise continued throughout the whole film.
The noise continued throughout the entire film.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **in**: It took her ten minutes to solve the puzzle.
answers: She solved the puzzle in ten minutes.

items.prompt: Во время отпуска я не проверял почту. (during)
answers: I didn't check my email during my holiday.
I did not check my email during my holiday.
I didn't check my email during the holiday.
I didn't check my emails during my holiday.
I didn't check my email during my vacation.
I didn't check my emails during my vacation.
I didn't check my email during my holidays.
I didn't check my emails during my holidays.
We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
We were waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
We waited twenty minutes for the bus.
We waited for the bus for 20 minutes.

items.prompt: Я буду ждать здесь, пока ты не позвонишь. (until)
answers: I'll wait here until you call.
I will wait here until you call.
I'll be waiting here until you call.
I will be waiting here until you call.
I'll wait here until you phone.
I'll wait here until you ring.

items.prompt: К пятнице отчёт должен быть готов. (by)
answers: The report must be ready by Friday.
The report has to be ready by Friday.
The report should be ready by Friday.
The report needs to be ready by Friday.
Prices have risen sharply over the past few years.
Prices have risen sharply over the last few years.
Prices have risen sharply in the past few years.
Prices have risen sharply in the last few years.

items.prompt: Она не засыпала до трёх часов ночи. (not ... until)
answers: She didn't fall asleep until 3 a.m.
She didn't fall asleep until three in the morning.
She didn't go to sleep until 3 a.m.
She didn't go to sleep until three in the morning.
She didn't get to sleep until 3 a.m.

items.prompt: How long have you been learning English? Use **for**.
items.sample: I have been learning English for about seven years.

items.prompt: What do you usually do during your lunch break?
items.sample: During my lunch break I usually go for a short walk.

items.prompt: What must you finish by the end of this week? Use **by**.
items.sample: I must finish a long report by the end of the week.

items.prompt: How late do you usually stay awake at the weekend? Use **until**.
items.sample: At the weekend I usually stay up until midnight.

items.prompt: What has changed in your life over the last few years?
items.sample: Over the last few years I have moved to a new city and changed jobs.
